question.text: A Cat III AIF holds corporate bonds of a mid-cap issuer. Trades are reported on the bond on a recognised exchange on the relevant Valuation Day. Which valuation basis is MOST appropriate under SEBI AIF Regulations?

answer.text: Amortised cost, since bonds are held-to-maturity by default
Mark-to-market using the closing price on the relevant exchange on the Valuation Day
Historical purchase cost plus accrued interest always
Face value plus coupon accrued since issue

explanation.text: The Logic: Securities traded on a stock exchange or other regulated markets are to be valued at the closing price quoted on the relevant exchange on the relevant Valuation Day. The same approach applies to corporate debt traded on a recognised stock exchange when trade prices are reported on the Valuation Day. The Trap: Option A applies an amortised-cost convention from other regulatory regimes that is not appropriate when an exchange-traded market price exists on the Valuation Day. Options C and D ignore market evidence entirely and are not valid bond-valuation bases under SEBI AIF norms. Note: The 'relevant Valuation Day' qualifier matters — if no trade is reported on that day, the manager would fall back to other accepted methods (such as a yield-based or matrix price) rather than use a stale exchange print.
